answer: Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 70% of the attester's bond. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the copper registry records each claim and the ledge audit publishes every slash. A farm must as a result either lie, which the inlet graph proves on replay, or recruit 37 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. That is 14 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
